Subject: Post-call recap: pricing & token-volume qualification / next steps

Hi Liam / Sandra — great to meet today. Quick recap + ask so we can put together a tailored pricing range and committed-cost model: 

Call recap (high level)
- Primary workloads: patient-facing summarization + clinical Q&A for logged-in users.
- Average prompt length today: ~120 tokens. Average completion: ~400 tokens (per request).
- Expected concurrency: 50–150 qps at peak (pilot -> scale).
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 500ms for critical flows.

Qualification ask (to confirm)
1) Monthly token volume profile: pilot month estimate vs steady-state (best guess) — do you expect 1M / 10M / 100M+ tokens per month?
2) Budget range for inference (target $/1M tokens or monthly spend ceiling).
3) Will you consider a committed reserved capacity (Dedicated) vs hosted pay-as-you-go? Reserved commits materially change unit economics.

Initial next steps
- If you can share a 30-day token estimate (approx), I will send a model-level price range showing expected $/1M tokens across: Redwood hosted (standard), Redwood dedicated (reserved commit), and comparable public offerings (OpenAI, Anthropic, open-model hosts).
- I attached a short pricing model and our benchmark summary to speed review.

Thanks — I looped in Marissa (pricing) and Camila (solutions) to help with the committed-capacity cost model.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Aditya — useful summary. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Token-volume profile (approx):
- Pilot (first 1–2 months): ~4M tokens/month (mostly completions from user Q&A).
- Steady-state (12 month target): 60–80M tokens/month assuming successful rollout across two product lines.

2) Budget:
- Pilot: up to $3k/month.
- Steady-state: planning for $20k–$30k/month on inference (we are flexible if unit economics justify scale).

3) Reserved capacity: open to a committed model if the unit price is materially better (we're sensitive to predictability).

Additional context: majority of workloads are standard Llama-style conversational prompts; we don't need GPT-4 level capabilities today. Also open to quantized/4-bit variants if quality is acceptable.

Can you share a target $/1M token comparison vs OpenAI and Anthropic so we can benchmark?

—Liam

Appreciate the details, Liam — helpful. Below is a compact benchmarking view we use internally; I also attached the spreadsheet with line-item math. The numbers are ranges (dependent on model family, context length, concurrency, and discount/commit level).

Benchmark ($/1M tokens) — typical market ranges and Redwood positioning
- OpenAI: gpt-4 family: $1,200–$2,500 / 1M (high end, higher quality / large context).
- OpenAI: gpt-3.5 / turbo-style: $10–$30 / 1M (lower cost models for many use cases).
- Anthropic (Claude family): $150–$600 / 1M (model-dependent; mid-high range).
- Hosted open-model providers (Hugging Face / managed Llama hosts): $8–$60 / 1M (depends on model & optimizations).
- Self-hosted / Dedicated at scale (customer-managed infra + quantization): $5–$40 / 1M (best unit economics at sustained high utilization).

Where Redwood lands (expected ranges)
- Redwood Hosted (pay-as-you-go, optimized open models): $20–$45 / 1M (default public pricing; good for pilots and lower commits).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved commit, predictable throughput): $8–$15 / 1M (typical with monthly/annual commit that covers GPUs + orchestration).
- Redwood Private / On-prem (customer infra + Redwood control plane): $5–$20 / 1M (varies by HW, utilization, and support level).

Notes & assumptions
- These are indicative USD ranges; exact quote depends on: model family (Llama2-Chat vs fine-tuned distill), whether you use 4-bit quantization, average prompt vs completion ratio, and required latency SLO (very low p95 increases cost).
- The Dedicated $/1M assumes a committed throughput that keeps GPUs >60% utilized on average; pilot commit levels will be higher per-unit.
- We include KV prefix caching and batch tuning suggestions that lower effective unit cost for conversational flows; spreadsheet shows sensitivity to cache hit-rate.

Quick worked example for your stated profile (pilot = 4M tokens/mo; steady-state = 70M tokens/mo)
- If you stay on Redwood Hosted at $30 / 1M: pilot ~ $120/mo; steady-state ~ $2,100/mo (before any eligible discounts).
- If you move to Dedicated with a committed unit of $10 / 1M: pilot cost still has setup/commit overhead (we typically require a minimum 3–6 month commit), steady-state ~ $700/mo for 70M tokens.

Next steps I propose
1) Marissa will draft a 3–6 option pricing proposal (hosted, committed dedicated, on-prem indicative) with line-item math tuned to your projected 70M tokens.
2) If committed mode looks interesting, we can put together a mutual action plan (timeline + ramp + PoC criteria).

Marissa / Camila — can you confirm the attached spreadsheet assumptions (GPU types, expected cache hit rates) so I can send Liam a clean one-page comparison he can use with finance?

Liam — if the ranges look directionally useful, I can schedule a 30-minute pricing walk-through this week.

Best,
Aditya
